title: Contracting intelligence meets legal intelligence
summary: Legora is the collaborative AI powering lawyers to review and research faster, draft smarter, and advise with precision. Legora adapts to your ways of working, unlocking team and machine collaboration at scale.
body_markdown:
Legal teams have always lived at the intersection of two bodies of knowledge: what the law says, and what their organization actually agreed to.


Those two things have never talked to each other.


Legal research tools know the law. Contract platforms know the contracts. But the insight that actually matters in a negotiation, a regulatory review, or a dispute—the one that says *here is how the law applies to what we signed* —has always required a person to sit between two systems and manually connect the dots.


That changes today.


Ironclad is announcing a partnership and AI-first product integration with Legora, the agentic operating system for legal work. Ironclad and Legora, who are mutual customers, bring together contracting intelligence from Ironclad and legal intelligence from Legora in one connected workflow, enabling the AI transformation of the full legal department.


## Two platforms that make each other smarter


Legora already knows the law. Ironclad already knows your contracts.


The integration connects them so neither platform is working from incomplete information.


Research in Legora gets better because it is now grounded in what your organization actually signed, not just what the statute says in the abstract. Redlining and risk flagging in Ironclad get better because every recommended position is backed by Legora’s legal research intelligence, not just a playbook rule last updated two years ago.


Ironclad and Legora do not just work side by side. They make each other smarter.


## What the integration does


**Access Ironclad contract intelligence inside Legora**


When you are working in Legora—conducting legal research, horizon scanning for upcoming regulatory changes—you can now ask questions about your Ironclad contracts and workflows without switching platforms.


For instance, while researching a new standard for California non-competes, you can look up how many of your executed employment agreements actually meet the requirements and how many will now need updating. Or, during M&A proceedings, you can run an analysis across the counterparty’s uploaded contracts to check non-standard clauses against EDGAR, SEC, and other public filings.


The answers come directly from your Ironclad repository. And soon, they’ll also come with citation snippets linking to the exact position in the source contract.


**Access Legora legal intelligence inside Ironclad**


When you are working in Ironclad reviewing a third-party agreement, preparing a redline, or evaluating risk, you can now research statutes, regulations, and case law with the context of the agreement in question.


Instead of opening a separate tab, running the research, and then trying to reconcile what you found with what is in front of you, the legal research is available right where the contracting work is already happening.


**Deep analysis and execution that round-trips**


With this integration, Ironclad and Legora will move from adjacent tools to one connected system.


Teams will be able to select executed contracts from Ironclad and run Legora’s Tabular Review across that full set. Tabular Review will extract key terms, flag gaps, and identify clauses that need attention after a regulatory change. Teams will then be able to bulk launch remediation workflows in Ironclad to execute the required changes at scale.


## What this looks like in practice


Let’s imagine that a counterparty presents new language to a commercial contracting attorney during a negotiation under the premise that it’s statutorily required in that specific jurisdiction. The attorney, who’s in Ironclad reviewing the agreement, uses Legora to pull up the relevant statute and then has Ironclad Agent propose the most appropriate redline, all without switching platforms or opening new tabs.


In that same legal department, a privacy attorney is researching privacy regulation changes for a key global market in Legora. Once she understands the impact of those changes, she uses Ironclad’s AI—within Legora—to assess the relevant contractual risk exposure to round out her understanding.


Insight is only part of the story, though; the team still needs to act upon it. Non-compliant agreements need to be flagged, their amendments need to be executed, and the resulting changes need to be documented and stored. So the privacy attorney pulls all the relevant agreements from Ironclad into Legora’s Tabular Review, which then identifies all the agreements that need amending and, critically, surfaces specific recommended amendment language for each agreement. Following the analysis, bulk workflows to amend each agreement get kicked off in Ironclad. They are fully executed—still adhering to pre-configured workflow rules, assignments, and approvals—and then added to the repository.


Instead of routing a question across practices, attorneys can follow it through, from research to amendment to execution, all without leaving their workflow.


## What this means for your legal team


**Legal research is grounded in what you actually signed**


Legora’s answers reflect both what the law requires and how your organization has actually handled it in executed agreements.


**Every risk flag in Ironclad is backed by the law**


When Ironclad’s Contract Review Agent surfaces a risk or recommends a redline, it now has access to Legora’s legal intelligence, so recommendations are grounded in current legal context, not just historical playbook positions.


**Your contract repository is searchable from inside your research workflow**


No more exporting documents, copying clause language, or manually reconstructing context. Your Ironclad contracts are accessible directly from Legora, with citation links back to the source.


**Large-scale analysis can drive action, not just findings**


[Tabular Review](https://legora.com/product/tabular-review) at scale is powerful. Connecting it to Ironclad’s workflow engine means the analysis does not stop at a spreadsheet—it becomes the starting point for remediation, re-negotiation, or renewal.


## Why we built this


Most legal teams we talk to are not missing research tools or contract platforms. They are missing the connection between them.


Legal AI has been built in silos: contracts get signed and sit unchecked while regulations evolve, research does not account for what the organization has already agreed to, and gaps only surface once a dispute forces everyone into a room together.


This partnership is designed to fix that, not by replacing the tools legal teams already use, but by making sure those tools share the context that makes them useful.


Moreover, Legora manages and negotiates its own agreements in Ironclad, while Ironclad conducts legal research and analysis in Legora. This tells you something about how each platform sees its role: Ironclad is the system of intelligence for contracting, and Legora is the AI layer for legal research. The integration reflects how teams actually work, not just how products are positioned.


Together, that is AI transformation for the whole legal department, in one connected workflow.


## What’s next


The integration is rolling out throughout the rest of this year. Phase one—Ironclad contracting intelligence accessible inside Legora—is in early access now, as is phase two, Legora legal intelligence inside Ironclad, with general availability targeted for this release cycle. Phase three, which includes deep analysis round-trip capabilities, is targeted for early access in the coming months.


If you are an existing customer of both platforms, reach out to your customer success team to get early access. If you want to learn more,[request a demo](https://legora.com/book-a-demo) or[explore the integration documentation](https://ironcladapp.com/product/integrations/legora) .


Because the best legal work happens when your research and your contracts are finally on the same page.
